title: My First Child's Birth Story
author: Noushin
body:
The day I gave birth to my first child was the most beautiful and unforgettable day of my life. It was a journey filled with fear, pain, excitement, love, and endless emotions that I will cherish forever.

It was one of those summer days when we decided to have a baby. I had so many wishes and plans for the baby. I always thought about how the baby was going to look, whether I could be a good mother, whether I was meeting his or her needs. There were so many questions like these.

Days passed. The fetus was just eight weeks old when one of my family members got sick. She needed surgery, but to perform the operation, someone had to donate blood, and there was no one to do it. I didn't know if I could donate blood or not. I didn't have a choice, so I got ready to donate blood and went to the hospital. Fortunately, the problem was solved and no surgery was needed. I became very happy. Two weeks later, I started having spotting and needed to rest for a while to keep the baby healthy. Everything went well, and the day to meet my beautiful angel was approaching.

One day when I came back from school at noon, I felt mild contractions and a little water. At first, I thought it was just normal discomfort, so I tried to continue with my daily routine. I just decided to go to my sister's home instead of my own. My mom was there. When she saw me, she asked about the position of the child. I answered that everything was normal, nothing special was happening. The hours passed. I didn't feel any change or strong pain, so I said goodbye to my mom and my sister Rabi and went home. It was a fasting month and my husband was fasting, so he broke his fast and we had dinner. During dinner, I spoke about my feelings to him, then we got ready to sleep. I felt the pain start becoming more regular but not strong. I preferred to go to the hospital, so Aziz took me there. As we got out of the home, we saw my mom getting out of a car, because she was worried about me and my baby. My mom came with us. Deep inside, I knew the moment we had been waiting for had finally arrived. I remember feeling both nervous and excited.

On the way to the hospital, my emotions were overwhelming. I looked out the car window thinking about how our lives were about to change forever. I wondered what my baby would look like, whose smile the baby would have, and whether I was truly ready to become a parent.

When we arrived at the hospital, the nurses quickly checked me and confirmed that I was in active labor. They said the baby would be born in half an hour, so my mom and my husband stayed at the hospital and waited to welcome the baby. But I didn't know what would happen later. Labor did not progress, and the contractions became more painful with each passing hour, but I kept reminding myself that every moment of pain was bringing me closer to meeting my child. It was ten PM when we arrived at the hospital. At 9 AM the doctor said it needed to be delivered by C-section. After the doctor left, the nurse who was with me tried her best to ensure that the baby was born naturally. The nurses were incredibly kind and supportive throughout the process. They encouraged me to stay strong and helped me feel safe and comfortable. They finally said the words I had been waiting to hear: "It's time to push." At that moment, I gathered all my strength. It was the hardest thing I had ever done, but also the most meaningful.

Then suddenly, my baby was born, but she was bruised and not crying. The nurses held the baby by the legs, head down, and gave her a few slaps until she cried. I heard the most beautiful sound in the world, my baby's first cry.

In that instant, all the pain disappeared. Tears filled my eyes as the nurses put my baby on my stomach during the stitches. Touching my child for the very first time felt magical. I looked at that face and immediately felt a love deeper than words could ever describe.

My heart was full of gratitude and happiness. I could not stop staring at my baby's little hands, tiny fingers, and peaceful face. It was hard to believe that this precious life had grown inside me for nine months. We named the baby Afra. She brought love and joy to our lives.

Becoming a mother changed my life forever. That day taught me the true meaning of unconditional love, strength, and sacrifice. Although labor was painful and exhausting, it was all worth it the moment I held my baby in my arms.

The birth of my first child will always remain the most special memory of my life, a story written in my heart forever.
